page: Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-2400s-amd is an AMD EPYC-powered server within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The processor architecture is x86_64, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 2400 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present.

In benchmark evaluations, this server demonstrates strong computational and memory performance. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance ranks in the top tier (top 10%), while multi-core stress-ng and PassMark CPU scores place in the strong top 25% tier. Memory subsystem performance is highly competitive, with PassMark memory scores reaching the top 10% and uncached read/write memory bandwidth tests consistently placing in the top 25%. For specialized workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds for small language models and strong text generation speeds for medium-sized models. Standard data processing tasks, such as gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and Redis SET operations, perform in the average middle 50% range.

Given its high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU and integrated 2400 GB NVMe SSD storage, this server offers excellent resource density for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads without the overhead of separate storage attachments. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable performance, avoiding the resource contention typical of shared-core environments. This profile is highly suited for memory-optimized databases, large-scale caching layers, data processing pipelines, and local LLM inference tasks that benefit from fast memory bandwidth and dedicated AMD EPYC execution units.
